Exact scalar minimization yields the two-phase radius/center/contact classification. For r=1 upper coordinate inequalities are not facets and are handled correctly. Independently checked boundary regimes and numeric samples n=9,16,20; finite checks are not the proof. All equations are mathematically valid.

originality.rationale: Two already published exact results jointly cover the entire claimed final statement, despite having different titles. The published general matroid independence-polytope minimum-sphere theorem gives for U_{r,n} the very same unique outer center, squared radius and contact vertices in its equations (2),(3)-(6),(11),(17). The published capped-hypercube John ellipsoid theorem analyzes exactly K_{n,tau}=[0,1]^n cap {sum x_i<=tau}, explicitly says integer tau are uniform-matroid independence polytopes, and establishes complete halfspace inclusion constraints s<=t, s<=1-t, nt+sqrt(n b)<=tau. Specializing to isotropic balls a=b=rho² (so s=rho) and symmetrizing centers gives rho<=min(t,1-t,(r-nt)/sqrt(n)); optimizing these displayed inequalities is a routine one-variable step yielding the inradius min(r/(n+sqrt(n)),1/2) and the same transition and tangent facets. Both components and their contact phases are therefore direct consequences of existing published results. Originality FAIL does not deny the submitted elementary proof.

final_claim: For 1<=r<n the uniform-matroid independence polytope I_{r,n}=[0,1]^n cap {sum x_i<=r} has unique Euclidean incenter and radius min(r/(n+sqrt(n)),1/2), with transition 2r=n+sqrt(n), and unique minimum-enclosing sphere centered at (r/n)*1 with squared radius r(n-r)/n for 2r<n or at (1/2)*1 with squared radius n/4 for 2r>=n, with the stated facet and contact-vertex phases.
